The second parodos of the chorus takes place, as is natural in the hot pursuit, ⟦1⟧; see in the Life of Aeschylus: ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, which, if that is to be relied upon, is to be referred first of all to the first parodos; yet the second is no different. So it was delivered by individuals or groups, as in the first parodos, which is also clearly shown; but the distribution is entirely unclear. Hermann gave the first 10 trimeters to the chorus leader; from 254 on he distinguishes 7 pieces, which he assigns to individual Erinyes. Strophic formation cannot occur here at all; moreover, the rhythms and meters (trimeters) are similar to those in the first parodos. Trimeters 261. 264.
